messages.subject: additive qtl
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
Am doing qtl mapping using the marker regression method. I then run
another scan using the largest qtl as an additive covariate. I
expected to see the second largest peak (if it is not linked to the
largest peak) as the additive qtl, but this is not the case. Often the
additive qtl is none of the qtls returned from scan one. Is it
possible there is a problem with my map or is my assumption wrong?
Musa.

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] additive qtl
messages.body_plain:
It's impossible to say whether there is a problem with your genetic map or not, and it's hard to say whether the results you are seeing are surprising or not.  How strong are the effects?

There is no guarantee that the second-highest peak will come up as most interesting once you condition on the first peak.  I would look at both the effect of that second-highest locus and also the association between genotypes at the two loci.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: additive qtl
messages.body_plain:
Genotypes at markers on different chromosomes would be expected to be
independent.  If the genotypes at the highest and 2nd highest peaks
are associated, that may indicate a problem with the genetic map, or
there could be something else going on, but in any case it explains
why, after conditioning on the highest peak, the evidence for a QTL at
the 2nd highest peak goes away.

karl

messages.subject: Questions concerning QTL variance and controlling for QTLs with major effect
messages.subject_clean: Questions concerning QTL variance and controlling for QTLs with major effect
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl

I would like to ask you the following:

- Could you please send me some feedback concerning the equation you
are using to estimate the percent variance explained by the QTL (R/QTL
book pg 77). For estimating the QTL effect the software is using the
same equation regardless of the method used for identifying the QTL?
Also how accurate you think it is this result.

- My second question concerns QTLs with major effect. I do not
understand why taking into account QTLs with major effects gives us
more power to detect QTLs in other chromosomes since we know
chromosomes segregate independently.

Kind Regards
Christos

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Questions concerning QTL variance and controlling for QTLs with major effect
messages.body_plain:
> - Could you please send me some feedback concerning the equation you
> are using to estimate the percent variance explained by the QTL (R/QTL
> book pg 77). For estimating the QTL effect the software is using the
> same equation regardless of the method used for identifying the QTL?
> Also how accurate you think it is this result.

It's true for a single QTL model, if you know the QTL genotypes (that is, the QTL is at a marker with no missing data).

It's approximately true for a single QTL model, with the QTL away from a marker, for any of the methods for dealing with missing genotype data.

It's approximately true for multiple QTL models in which the QTL models are additive and unlinked, when the LOD is interpreted in the equation is interpreted as a conditional LOD, RSS1 is for the full model, and RSS0 is for the model in which the QTL of interest is omitted.

The equation isn't at all correct when there are linked QTL.  That's a major problem with the fitqtl function, but I don't currently have a solution.

> - My second question concerns QTLs with major effect. I do not
> understand why taking into account QTLs with major effects gives us
> more power to detect QTLs in other chromosomes since we know
> chromosomes segregate independently.

If you ignore the major QTL, the variation due to that QTL is included in the residual variance when you search for additional QTL.

karl

messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl

Thanks for the reply.

Concerning my second question i wanted to ask you the following:

For example in the second case study of your book (pg 324) you run
scanone and you identify a major QTL in chromosome 8 and 3 others in
different chromosomes. By controlling for the major QTL and rerunning
the analysis you find evidence for two additional QTLs, which you did
not see in the first case. I am not really sure why this is the case
since at the same time you consider that the permutation tests of
single QTL models apply for other models as well due to independent
segregation distortion (R/QTL book pg 312).

Thanks

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Re: Questions concerning QTL variance and controlling for QTLs with major effect
messages.body_plain:
I don't see what else I can add.  If you control for major QTL, you can reduce residual variation and so increase your power to detect further QTL.

Applying the results of permutation tests for a single-QTL model to other models with more QTL is an approximation that seems to work.

karl
